From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Onramp: HelioBank POC charter & evaluation approach

Hi Sara / Paul — great call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth as we scope the onramp for HelioBank. Attached: HelioBank_POC_Charter_v1.pdf (charter + timeline) and a starter rubric.

Key priorities you mentioned:
- Integrate Redwood Inference for customer support routing and risk detection (exact flows: claims routing + fraud flagging)
- Keep PII inside your VPC (on-prem / private deployment evaluation)
- Demonstrate parity on accuracy vs current rule set and show predictable latency under load

Proposed success criteria (draft):
1) Accuracy uplift or parity: automated labels match or exceed baseline on a stratified sample (target F1 >= 0.78)
2) Operational SLOs: 95th pct latency < 350ms for single-message inference
3) False-positive control: precision on fraud flags >= 0.85 on production-like distribution
4) Security gate: SOC2 evidence & network model placement validated

Evaluation approach (high level):
- Phase A (offline baseline): Redwood runs an offline evaluation on a sanitized sample you provide (3–5k records) to benchmark model variants.
- Phase B (shadowing): 2-week shadow run against live traffic in your staging VPC (no customer-visible actions, logging only).
- Decision point: If offline + shadow meet thresholds we move to a short production pilot with a rollback plan.

Immediate asks from HelioBank to move forward:
- A sanitized sample export window (approx 5k records) and data schema by EOD next Tue (2027-09-21)
- Confirmation if Security wants a separate evidence package or an on-call session

Owners we propose: Redwood PM: Marissa Cole (owner); Redwood SRE/Infra: Ben Carter (shadow run lead); Redwood ML Ops: Karthik Iyer (offline evaluation & rubric).

Next steps:
1) Sara / Paul: confirm data export window + security contact
2) Redwood: finalize rubric and timeline (attached) and send SOW/statement of work link

Thanks — I’ll follow up with an updated charter once I get your confirmation.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Marissa — quick internal proposal from my side (technical owner perspective):

Summary: Recommend a hybrid evaluation: 1 week offline (sanitized sample) + 2 week shadow in staging VPC. Rationale: offline helps narrow model choices and surface labeling gaps; shadow validates latency and distribution shift under live traffic without customer impact.

Proposed thresholds (recommendation):
- Offline F1 target: >= 0.78 on stratified sample
- Precision on flagged fraud: >= 0.85 (measured on a 2k holdout where fraud labels exist)
- Shadow latency SLO: p95 < 350ms, p99 < 600ms (in staging with traffic replay)
- Production pilot acceptance: combined score >= 0.80 (see rubric column mapping)

Owners and runbook:
- Offline eval lead: Karthik (prepare data spec + offline run)
- Shadow run lead: Ben (infrastructure + logging + KV cache validation)
- PM owner: Marissa (stakeholder comms + decision)

Timeline (tentative):
- Week 0 (kickoff): finalize data spec + security NDA + SOW
- Week 1: offline run on sanitized sample; compare 3 model variants and produce report
- Week 2–3: shadow run in staging VPC (2 weeks)
- Week 4: decision meeting + small production pilot if accepted

Notes on data: we’ll need a minimal schema and a small example CSV. If HelioBank needs help redacting PII we can provide a simple transform script under an NDA.

I’ll draft a one-page runbook and attach to the charter update.

—
Ben Carter
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
